request.what: Reduce the Cardano protocol parameter committeeMinSize from 7 to 5.

claims.claim: The proposal changes the minimum Constitutional Committee size parameter from 7 to 5.
The current Constitutional Committee comprises 7 members, equal to the current committeeMinSize setting of 7.

A single resignation or term expiration under the current setting would put the committee below committeeMinSize and make governance actions requiring Constitutional Committee approval ineligible for ratification.
Reducing committeeMinSize to 5 would create an operational buffer so governance can continue if one or two members retire or their terms expire, assuming a current 7-member body.

The proposal states that its enactment depends temporally on another live Parameter Change governance action for Plutus cost model settings, with no technical interaction between the parameter changes.
The proposal does not directly affect the current number of Constitutional Committee members and does not change the maximum number of committee members.
With a 2/3 Constitutional Committee voting threshold, the proposal states that 5 members require 4 constitutional votes to meet threshold and 2 unconstitutional votes can prevent threshold.
The proposal acknowledges that at a committee size of 5, inactivity of one member would allow another member to fully veto governance actions.
The proposal states the change underwent technical review through the Parameter Committee Parameter Change Process and links to the PCP-005 Cardano Forum discussion.

The proposal says the change is reversible if there are at least 7 Constitutional Committee members, but reverting to 7 while fewer than 7 members are seated would immediately halt governance until sufficient members were elected.

summary: The document proposes a non-treasury parameter change to reduce committeeMinSize from 7 to 5, arguing this improves governance resilience against committee vacancies while preserving safeguards, with an acknowledged veto/inactivity tradeoff at smaller committee size and a conditional reversion plan.
